Court of Justice of the European Union

JUDGMENT OF THE COURT (Grand Chamber)

Keywords

Data protection — Transfer of personal data to third countries

Summary

1. The examination of the validity of Commission Decision 2010/87/EU reveals no factor of such a kind as to affect its validity.

2. The Court holds that the standard contractual clauses are valid mechanisms for data transfers.

Parties

Data Protection Commissioner v Facebook Ireland Limited and Maximillian Schrems

Subject of the case

Request for a preliminary ruling concerning the interpretation of Articles 46 and 58 of Regulation 2016/679.

Grounds

1. By its questions, the referring court asks, in essence, whether the GDPR applies to transfers of personal data.

2. In that regard, it must be noted that Regulation (EU) 2016/679 lays down rules relating to the protection of natural persons.

3. The Court has already held that the level of protection must be essentially equivalent.

4. It follows from the foregoing that the transfer mechanisms must ensure adequate safeguards.

5. Article 46 of Regulation 2016/679 provides for appropriate safeguards.

An unnumbered concluding remark about the legal framework.

Decision on costs

Since these proceedings are, for the parties to the main proceedings, a step in the action pending before the referring court, the decision on costs is a matter for that court.

Operative part

1. Article 46(1) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 must be interpreted as meaning that the appropriate safeguards provided for may be ensured by standard data protection clauses.

2. Article 6 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 applies to the processing of personal data in the context of transfer mechanisms.

3. The decision is declared invalid. Article 6 of Regulation 2016/679 requires a valid legal basis.
